cards.front: What should you know about ao3 weighting?
cards.back: Context is worth 15-25% of marks. Always link context to specific analysis, never just list facts.

cards.front: What should you know about caution?
cards.back: Don't reduce poems to autobiography. Use biography to illuminate, not define meaning.

cards.front: What should you know about never bolt context on?
cards.back: "This poem was written in 1917 during WW1. Owen shows..." Integrate context: "Owen's graphic imagery of 'gargling blood' reflects the brutal reality of trench warfare, challenging the patriotic lies told to families at home."

cards.front: What should you know about top tip?
cards.back: AO3 (context) is worth 15-25% of poetry marks depending on your exam board. Context must be integrated into your analysis — never bolt it on as a separate paragraph. Every context point should be linked to a specific quotation or technique. A single well-integrated context point outperforms three disconnected facts.
Trench warfare, shell shock (e.g. Anti-war poetry, graphic realism)
Depression, suicide attempts (e.g. Confessional poetry, intense emotion)
Working-class London, visionary (e.g. Social criticism, mystical imagery)
Nature, emotion, individual (e.g. Wordsworth, Keats, Shelley)
Formal structure, moral purpose (e.g. Tennyson, Browning, Arnold)
Personal experience, taboo subjects (e.g. Plath, Sexton, Lowell)

cards.front: What does AQA Power and Conflict mean?
cards.back: Power, its abuse, conflict (e.g. Ozymandias, My Last Duchess, War Photographer)

cards.front: What does AQA Love and Relationships mean?
cards.back: Love in various forms (e.g. Porphyria's Lover, Sonnet 29, Neutral Tones)

cards.front: What does Edexcel Time and Place mean?
cards.back: Landscape, identity, memory (e.g. Various location-based poems)

cards.front: What does Bolting on context facts mean?
cards.back: Link every context point to a quotation
